scope: Document 03 conceptual domain model; no baseline/implementation assertion

profile.title: Professional profile
profile.meaning: Reusable private professional source information, distinct from published presentation.

entry.title: Professional entry
entry.meaning: Experience, education, skill or professional-project information; categories do not select implementation subclasses.

resume.title: Tailored resume
resume.meaning: Independent opportunity-specific selections, wording and presentation.
resume.actions: Compose; apply selected changes; request publication

selection.title: Source selection
selection.meaning: Meaning of selecting source information for one resume, without automatic propagation.

override.title: Resume-specific override
override.meaning: Independent wording/presentation belonging to the intended resume.

evidence.title: Supporting evidence
evidence.meaning: Externally authored text, media, files, diagrams or links supporting skills or professional projects.

evidencechoice.title: Evidence selection
evidencechoice.meaning: Deliberate per-resume disclosure, distinct from evidence existence.

language.title: Language-specific content
language.meaning: Manually maintained English/German text in its relevant source/resume context.

publication.title: Published presentation
publication.meaning: Owner-confirmed effective presentation, semantically distinct from the draft; not a mandatory snapshot table.

generated.title: Generated resume PDF
generated.meaning: Derived rendition with identifiable represented content and language.

uploaded.title: Uploaded resume PDF
uploaded.meaning: Independently prepared PDF associated with the intended resume and language.

download.title: PDF download availability
download.meaning: Per-resume generated/uploaded/both/neither choice with applicable language availability.

link.title: Protected employer link
link.meaning: Password-protected scoped presentation access without a viewer account; not verified employer identity.
link.attrs: Target context; access state; credential control

company.title: Company
company.meaning: Organization information for private application work; no global public directory is implied.

opportunity.title: Job opportunity
opportunity.meaning: Position being considered, distinct from the application process for it.

application.title: Application record
application.meaning: Manual preparation and progress context relating an opportunity to intended materials.

letter.title: Cover letter
letter.meaning: Manually authored editable application text, distinct from its actual submitted copy.

submission.title: Submission record
submission.meaning: User-recorded actual submission and completeness context, not proof of receipt.

material.title: Preserved submitted material
material.meaning: Identifiable actual submitted resume/cover-letter material independent of later live changes.

connection.title: Provider connection
connection.meaning: Selected user/provider identity and authorized capabilities; product login is not Google consent.

message.title: Email message / draft
message.meaning: Correspondence with provider message/thread identity and truthful save/send outcomes.

activity.title: Calendar activity
activity.meaning: Local activity or explicitly related provider event with meaningful time and authority.

reminder.title: Activity reminder
reminder.meaning: Notification intent for an authorized activity; scheduling is not demonstrated delivery.

project.title: Work project
project.meaning: Authorized work organization, distinct from professional projects and Git repositories.

board.title: Board
board.meaning: Organized work view, not another Product or Sprint Backlog.

column.title: Board column
column.meaning: Configured display organization whose movement rules agree with actual work states.

backlog.title: Product Backlog
backlog.meaning: Ordered planned outcomes/work in an authorized work context.

item.title: Backlog Item
item.meaning: Planned outcome with criteria; not interchangeable with a Task or repository Issue.

task.title: Task
task.meaning: Specific activity contributing to work with its own assignment/completion meaning.

sprint.title: Sprint
sprint.meaning: Work period with goal and actual outcome; elapsed time does not imply success.

sprintbacklog.title: Sprint Backlog
sprintbacklog.meaning: One coherent meaning comprising goal, selected Backlog Items and delivery plan.
sprintbacklog.actions: Select work; adapt plan; retain outcome

repo.title: Git repository
repo.meaning: Real hosted content/history under repository-specific authority.

revision.title: Git revision
revision.meaning: Identified repository content/history state used in browsing, review and execution.

ref.title: Git reference
ref.meaning: Named branch or tag associated with Git history; ref names differ from identified revisions.

pr.title: Pull request
pr.meaning: Proposed integration with explicit source/target repository/ref and evaluated revision context.

review.title: Review / comment
review.meaning: Attributed discussion/review of an intended request/revision, not universal merge permission.

issue.title: Repository issue
issue.meaning: Repository work/discussion record distinct from a work-project Backlog Item.

milestone.title: Repository milestone
milestone.meaning: Repository planning checkpoint for related issue work.

release.title: Release record
release.meaning: Named release tied to intended Git state and protected assets; not deployment authorization.

workflow.title: Workflow definition
workflow.meaning: Supported YAML behavior at identified definition/code context; validation is not execution.

run.title: Workflow run
run.meaning: Authorized execution request with evaluated code/definition and actual result context.

attempt.title: Execution attempt
attempt.meaning: Candidate retry/execution distinction so earlier failed/unknown work is not silently rewritten.

output.title: Run output
output.meaning: Logs/artifacts attributable to a producing execution context with protected access/lifecycle.
output.actions: Expose permitted output; clean eligible data

secret.title: Scoped secret authority
secret.meaning: Permission to use a secret for a specific repository/event/target; no secret values are modeled.

deployment.title: Deployment authorization
deployment.meaning: Separate explicit approval for target and exact revision/artifact, not implied by a successful run.

target.title: Deployment target
target.meaning: Intended environment whose effects and recovery conditions require review.

account.title: User account
account.meaning: Individual application identity and account state; role names do not grant universal access.

grant.title: Resource authority
grant.meaning: Role/permission, invitation or membership meaning for actor/resource/action/state; not an ACL schema.

file.title: Protected file resource
file.meaning: Admitted content identity with its domain access/reference meaning; not a common storage engine.

policy.title: File/storage policy
policy.meaning: Effective admission/accounting rules within an evaluated resource envelope.

audit.title: Operational evidence
audit.meaning: Restricted evidence of selected sensitive/administrative outcomes, not blanket content logging.
audit.actions: Record specified evidence; inspect permitted records

backup.title: Backup/recovery record
backup.meaning: Identity, coverage and access context of recoverable material; existence is not restoration proof.

restore.title: Restoration assessment
restore.meaning: Evaluation of restored integrity, access and external-state reconciliation.

accepted_core: Q-D07 core: no automatic resume/live changes; preview/selected apply; separate publication; preserve actual submitted documents

legacy_diagrams.name: domain-professional-presentation
legacy_diagrams.title: Professional information and independent tailoring
legacy_diagrams.basis: PRP-D01 PRP-D02 PRP-D03 PRP-D04 PRP-D05 PRP-D06 PRP-D07 PRP-D09
legacy_diagrams.description: Source selection, independent override and evidence selection answer different questions: what is reused, what is tailored and what is disclosed. Selection/override boxes can become values or association properties; they are not mandated database entities. Evidence support targets the skill/professional-project subjects in the grouped entry box, not automatically every entry category.
legacy_diagrams.questions: Q-D06/Q-D08/Q-D09 remain proposals. Profile count, required fields, language fallback and evidence-removal behavior are not finalized. Accepted Q-D07 core behavior applies directly.

legacy_diagrams.name: domain-publication-and-sharing
legacy_diagrams.title: Publication, representations and protected sharing
legacy_diagrams.basis: PRP-D04 PRP-D08 PDF-D01 PDF-D02 PDF-D03 PDF-D04 PDF-D05 PDF-D06 PDF-D07
legacy_diagrams.description: Published presentation differs from editable resume content. Generated and uploaded PDFs have different provenance; no shared implementation superclass is selected. Changing PDF availability and disabling a link remain independent operations.
legacy_diagrams.questions: Q-D10/Q-D11 retain detailed generation/revision/language/link proposals. This model does not accept link count, expiry, exact session-revocation timing, retained revision count or rendering technology.

legacy_diagrams.name: domain-applications-and-communication
legacy_diagrams.title: Applications, submitted history and communication
legacy_diagrams.basis: APP-D01 APP-D02 APP-D03 APP-D04 APP-D05 APP-D06 APP-D07 APP-D08 EGC-D01 EGC-D05 EGC-D07 EGC-D08 EGC-D10 EGC-D11
legacy_diagrams.description: Preparation, actual submission recording and provider operations have independent meanings. An application refers to its intended resume, while preserved materials identify what was actually submitted. A provider connection does not make every activity remote or every application send mail.
legacy_diagrams.questions: Q-D12–Q-D17 retain progress, capture/correction, synchronization and uncertain-result proposals. OAuth is not created; this diagram does not assert provider access or delivery.

legacy_diagrams.name: domain-work-management
legacy_diagrams.title: Work projects, backlogs, boards and Sprints
legacy_diagrams.basis: PKS-D01 PKS-D02 PKS-D03 PKS-D04 PKS-D05 PKS-D06 PKS-D07 PKS-D08 PKS-D09 PKS-D10
legacy_diagrams.description: A board presents work; it is not a second backlog. A Backlog Item expresses an outcome and acceptance meaning, while a Task expresses an activity. One Sprint Backlog comprises goal, selected items and delivery plan. Product work management differs from the board used to develop Resumefolio.
legacy_diagrams.questions: Q-D18–Q-D20 propose project/backlog counts, task-parent constraints, canonical states, at most one active Sprint and cross-module links. No mandatory cadence, team or extra delivery staff is inferred.

legacy_diagrams.name: domain-git-collaboration
legacy_diagrams.title: Real Git and repository collaboration
legacy_diagrams.basis: GIT-D01 GIT-D02 GIT-D03 GIT-D04 GIT-D05 GIT-D06 GIT-D07 GIT-D08 GIT-D09
legacy_diagrams.description: Repository identity, refs and identified revisions are separated so review, merge and execution cannot rely on an ambiguous moving branch name. A fork is another repository with explicit provenance and authority, not an inherited access grant. Issues/milestones differ from work-project items.
legacy_diagrams.questions: Q-D21/Q-D22 retain transport, credential, protection, review and merge proposals. No Git engine, merge strategy or public-visibility policy is selected.

legacy_diagrams.name: domain-execution-and-deployment
legacy_diagrams.title: Workflow execution and separate deployment authority
legacy_diagrams.basis: YML-D01 YML-D02 YML-D03 YML-D04 YML-D05 YML-D06 YML-D07 YML-D08 YML-D09 YML-D10 YML-D11 YML-D12
legacy_diagrams.description: Validation, run request, actual execution, output and deployment approval remain distinct. Run/attempt is a provisional decomposition for retries and unknown outcomes. Deployment approval names target and exact artifact/revision; job code cannot grant itself that authority.
legacy_diagrams.questions: Q-D23 remains evidence-gated. Syntax, limits, job/step detail, run/attempt structure and isolation need review/evidence. Real execution remains in scope but is not enabled or proven by this diagram; no runner is placed on the existing host.

legacy_diagrams.name: domain-access-files-and-recovery
legacy_diagrams.title: Shared access, files and recoverable operation
legacy_diagrams.basis: ACC-D01 ACC-D03 ACC-D05 ACC-D09 ACC-D10 ACC-D12 AFO-D01 AFO-D02 AFO-D03 AFO-D04 AFO-D06 AFO-D10 QSR-D10 QSR-D11 QSR-D12 QSR-D13
legacy_diagrams.description: Resource authority applies across domain resources; the file edge is an example. Protected file resource is a shared access/reference meaning, not a requirement that Git objects, mail attachments and resume files use one storage engine or quota pool. Recovery records are not public presentation artifacts.
legacy_diagrams.questions: Q-D03–Q-D05 and Q-D24–Q-D27 retain detailed grants, quota applicability, retention and operational proposals. Backups are not configured; a backup record cannot substitute for demonstrated restoration.
